items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: playing alto and clarinet, that you were first of all in the Hampton Sextet, a group which included pianist Sir Charles Thompson... Is that right? That's correct.

ctx.x: His nickname was "Mushmouth." Milt Buckner (PHONETIC) ended up being the regular pianist with the Hampton band, after Sir Charles Thompson (PHONETIC), who was the first beginner. We had a fellow by the name of Vernon Alley (bass) who was a staunch San Franciscoan. He came out of San Francisco for the first and only time in his life with that band and rushed right back home and immediately stayed there for the rest of his life, which he's still living. Of course, he was with our Navy band, of which I was the…
We had a 45-piece military band. I was the leader of the swing band called the Bombadiers, which was a 17-piece band. Vernon Alley was bass player in that particular band.

items.title: 68437_Charles Thompson oral history interview
items.q: So he recommended me to Lionel Hampton, and I joined his band... And Marshall Royal, saxophonist and clarinetist... But the basic group was made up of Marshall Royal... and myself on piano.

ctx.x: So he recommended me to Lionel Hampton, and I joined his band after he left Benny Goodman. Well, in that band was -- well, you know, Illinois Jacquet who I later on played with, that song 'Robin's Nest.' And Marshall Royal, saxophonist and clarinetist. He played violin. Do you want to know the name of that band?
